questions.question: What clinical features in this young patient—including BMI, family history, autoantibody status, and C-peptide results—suggested MODY rather than type 1 or type 2 diabetes, and what features made the distinction from type 2 diabetes particularly challenging?

HNF1A encodes a transcription factor expressed in the liver, kidneys, and pancreas. How do loss-of-function mutations in HNF1A lead to progressive beta-cell dysfunction, and which specific downstream target genes and enzymatic activities are impaired?

Patients with HNF1A-MODY often present with glycosuria at lower blood glucose levels than expected. What molecular mechanism accounts for this reduced renal threshold for glucose, and how does it relate to the tissue expression pattern of HNF1A?

SGLT2 inhibitors are generally avoided in patients with HNF1A-MODY. What is the pathophysiologic rationale for this caution, and what specific clinical complications have been described in this population?
What is the recommended first-line pharmacologic treatment for HNF1A-MODY, and how does its mechanism of action directly address the underlying beta-cell defect?

The glucagon stimulation test was used in this case to assess residual beta-cell function, showing a stimulated C-peptide level of 0.83 nmol/L. What does this value indicate about endogenous insulin secretion, and how does this test help differentiate MODY from type 1 diabetes?

The MODY probability calculator from the Exeter group estimated a 62.4% probability of MODY in this patient. What are the key limitations of this calculator when applied to non-White populations, and why might BMI and metabolic syndrome be increasingly unreliable for distinguishing MODY from type 2 diabetes?

After genetic confirmation of HNF1A-MODY, insulin was discontinued and replaced with dulaglutide, a GLP-1 receptor agonist. What clinical trial evidence supports the use of GLP-1 receptor agonists in HNF1A-MODY, and what advantages do they offer over sulfonylureas?

The novel HNF1A variant in this case (p.N270S, c.809A>G) was classified as likely pathogenic according to ACMG guidelines despite being absent from ClinVar and other variant databases. What specific lines of genetic and clinical evidence supported this pathogenicity classification?
